direction: Evolve the single hook `score_ruin_nodes` into a capacity-tightness-aware multiplicative gating + rank-power ruin priority: score_i = rank_power(|removal_savings_i| / scale * gate_load * gate_depot * gate_demand * gate_rdist, p(iter_frac, stagnation_ratio)), where gate_load emphasises nodes on high-fill-ratio routes (capacity_level=tight regimes), gate_rdist emphasises nodes on long/geometrically stretched routes (size=100 + eccentric depot), and the exponent p escalates from ~1.0 (intensification, low stagnation) to ~2.0-2.5 (diversification, high stagnation_ratio) so the anytime LNS keeps a monotone improving anytime_curve within the 500 ms deadline.

operations.mechanism: Round-4 champion (15.9986, 268 ms) shows headroom: archive VBS is 381.83 vs SBS 383.97 (gap over VBS 0.56%), so gains must come from per-instance specialization rather than a single fixed rule. KB method-cvrp-m3-ruin-recreate-l3 documents the exact multi-hour-verified hook contract and confirms (a) scale-normalized removal_savings as the base signal, (b) multiplicate load/depot/demand/route-distance gates, and (c) a rank-power exponent driven by iter_frac and stagnation_ratio beat Worst-Cost Removal (23.3186 vs 23.3474) on blind_120; it also warns that per-iteration reinsertion cost must stay inside the unified deadline, which the 268 ms round-4 mean leaves ample room under 500 ms. Weakest-regime report identifies tight capacity (vbs_rel_gap -22.68%), size 100 (-21.49%), clustered spatial (-19.51%) and eccentric depot (-20.55%) as the largest unfilled gaps, which the load gate and route-distance gate directly target. Only the single allowed hook is touched (postprocess_mode=none), so the 5-gate InterfaceValidator causal probe on the fixed 6-customer set remains satisfied deterministically.

preserve: Route feasibility, strict time budget, and scale invariance.
hypothesis: On cvrp_dev_hetero_24 at 500 ms, a multiplicative-gated rank-power ruin score that weights route fill-ratio and route-distance exposure (both normalized by within-instance scale) and raises its rank exponent with stagnation_ratio will lower mean tour length below the current SBS 15.9986, with the largest per-instance gains concentrated in the weakest regimes (capacity_level=tight, size=100, spatial=clustered, depot_style=eccentric), because removing near-capacity and long-route nodes creates the highest-value reinsertion recombinations there while stagnation escalation prevents premature convergence at the ~2-3 ms first_feasible anchor.
